rv.q: This is a witty production that finds an interesting new slant of power struggle inflected by gender.
As the revelations and explanations arrive one after the other, Tang and company make the story’s contradictions something to celebrate.
Maybe it is lesser performed for good reason, or perhaps this production, full of inspired ideas, does not anchor them down enough.
The sprawling play displays its customary capacity to snare attention; we allow the far-fetched flourishes while the drops of heartfelt speech (“Hang there, like fruit, my soul…”) work a treat.
She has a solid grasp of a slippery play.
They give depth and flavour to a mediocre script.

cn.t: Mixed reviews greet this gender-swapped Cymbeline at the Sam Wanamaker. Critics appreciate the bold reimagining of Shakespeare's rarely-staged sprawler, but find the production uneven despite its inventive matriarchal twist.
